newsitem.title: CROATIA: Zagreb bourse says on-line trading system started.
newsitem.headline: Zagreb bourse says on-line trading system started.

text.p: The Zagreb Stock Exchange, Croatia's central bourse, said on Wednesday it had started a new on-line trading system TEST-1.5 SV this week.
So far only 14 of the current 45 member brokerages have a direct connection with the the central computer, but there are plans to hook up all of them by year-end, the bourse said in a statement.
Other brokers will continue to trade via modem on the old off-line system, which will remain in use until then.
The new link, suited to existing telecommunications networks in Croatia, enables quicker communication between traders and is expected to increase the number of transactions.
It was said to be a step toward introducing more advanced software for automatic matching in about a year's time.
TEST-1.5 SV was developed by a Croatian electronics team under the guidance of the exchange's own engineer Davorin Rusevljan, using international standards.

The costs of creating it were said to have been much lower than the purchase of such a system abroad that would have made the bourse dependent on foreign technology, possibly hampering its further development.
"In this way the Zagreb Stock Exchange provides its members with top technology for trade at a minimal fee," it said.
